thread:
maria: Heads-up: the k6 replay for the customer spike tomorrow is showing a capacity mismatch on staging — lots of 429s and some orphaned sessions. Can we triage?

kevin: Where are the 429s coming from? gateway or runtime?

sre-bot: Alert: 429 rate increased by 7x on runtime-prod (route /v1/generate) over the last 10m — sample IDs attached.

maria: This was from a controlled replay against the dedicated pool in staging (burst profile). The gateway is returning 429s when downstream pods are saturated, but the runtime also logs the KV cache thrashing. Seeing many sessions that never close (ws client timeouts).

alex: I suspect the k6 arrival rate + per-connection throttle is too aggressive for the current autoscaler policy. We should try lowering the test's arrival rate and enable connection pacing. Quick config suggestion:

```
import http from 'k6/http';
export let options = {
  stages: [ {duration: '3m', target: 400}, {duration: '12m', target: 1200}, {duration: '10m', target: 1200} ],
  thresholds: { 'http_req_duration': ['p(95)<800'] },
  ext: { loadimpact: { projectID: 12345 } }
};
// use --rps to cap arrival if needed: k6 run --rps 1500 script.js
```

alex: Also add a KV cache warmup phase and set `--rps` to cap bursts.

jess: Can we do a quick dry run with 50% traffic and the rps cap? I can profile the runtime traces and check thread stacks.

sam: I can tweak the Dedicated autoscaler policy: lower scale-down threshold, increase min pods by 2 for the window. Will schedule the change for a 30m window before the replay.

maria: Thanks. Kevin, can you paste any recent runtime logs showing orphaned sessions? A stack sample would help.

kevin: Pasted a small snippet from staging logs:

```
[2026-03-15T14:02:11Z] WARN kvcache: miss_rate=0.87 pid=7fdc4 thread=12
[2026-03-15T14:02:12Z] ERROR session: websocket timeout, id=56f3a, state=idle last_active=110s
[2026-03-15T14:02:12Z] INFO tokens: emit=1200 latency_p50=120ms p95=860ms
[2026-03-15T14:02:12Z] WARN backpressure: active_workers=96 max_workers=100
```

kevin: Looks like workers are saturated and cleanup GC isn't keeping up.

olivia: Quick ask — if we cap RPS, should we also reduce per-request token window? Some of the high-latency calls are huge prompts. Maybe set an L7 rule to reject >2k token requests during test.

alex: Good call. Add a temporary routing policy: reject requests with token_count>2000 during replay and route overflow to a cheaper model variant. Example envoy header match + rate limit.

maria: Plan: 1) Sam applies min-pods bump and short autoscaler tweak 2) Alex/kevin run a 20-min dry run at 50% with --rps cap and KV warmup 3) Jess collects profiler stacks and traces 4) Olivia adds token reject rule + fallback route 5) Run full replay with ramp for 30m and monitor 429s and orphaned sessions metric.

sam: I'll apply autoscaler change at 09:15 PT and revert after 2h if stable.

jess: I'll start the dry run at 09:35 PT and post flame graphs here.

maria: If anything unexpected, tag @oncall and drop perf-trace links. Also, leave a small rollback playbook in the replay run notes.

kevin: Noted. Uploading trace collector command: `curl -X POST https://staging-ops.internal/trace-collect -d '{"since": 2026-03-15T14:00:00Z, "level": "debug"}'`

olivia: I'll prepare the envoy rule and a temporary policy in the console.

maria: Great — thanks all. I'll update the run doc and add the checklist. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Deploy scheduled: autoscaler-change by sam at 2026-03-16T09:15:00Z.

maria: Closing loop — post-run we'll validate regression checks (p95 latency, 429 rate, orphaned_session_count) and decide whether to keep autoscaler changes.
